description: Complete SDK method surface for @pushchain/core and @pushchain/ui-kit: all namespaces, method signatures, parameter types, return types, and safe_for_autonomous_execution flags. For intent-level capability definitions (what an agent can do) see capabilities.json. For routing logic see decision-tree.json and task-router.md.

methods.name: READ
methods.description: Universal Read constants. READ.OUTCOME is the success signal on each response (SUCCESS, SOURCE_ERROR, CALLBACK_FAILED, DECODE_FAILED, EXPIRED, FAILED, ABORTED, PENDING, UNKNOWN); READ.ERROR_CODE explains raw.errorCode (INVALID_QUERY, UNSUPPORTED, REVERTED, NOT_FOUND, INVALID_RESULT, REJECTED). READ.STATUS is the request lifecycle (PENDING, VOTING, FULFILLED, EXPIRED, FAILED, ABORTED); READ.RESULT_STATUS is what the source returned (SUCCESS or ERROR); READ.UNIVERSAL_READ_REGISTRY_ADDRESS.TESTNET_DONUT is the Universal Read Registry (0x00000000000000000000000000000000000000b2). Full values in agents/constants.json.

methods.name: getMoveableTokens

methods.name: getPayableTokens

methods.name: getPRC20Address
methods.signature: PushChain.utils.tokens.getPRC20Address(token: MoveableToken | { chain: CHAIN, address: string }, options?: { network?: PUSH_NETWORK }): { address: `0x${string}`; chain: CHAIN; symbol: string; decimals: number; network: PUSH_NETWORK }
methods.description: Returns the full PRC-20 token descriptor on Push Chain corresponding to a moveable token (address, chain, symbol, decimals, network). PRC-20 = a token born on an EXTERNAL chain, mirrored inward as a synthetic on Push Chain (USDC.eth, pETH). Synchronous — resolved from the SDK's static token table. For tokens born ON Push Chain (PC-20), use the async getPC20Address instead.
methods.returns: { address: `0x${string}`; chain: CHAIN; symbol: string; decimals: number; network: PUSH_NETWORK }

methods.name: getPC20Address
methods.signature: PushChain.utils.tokens.getPC20Address(address: string, options: { network: PUSH_NETWORK; chain?: CHAIN; rpcUrls?: Partial<Record<CHAIN, string[]>>; strict?: boolean }): Promise<PC20AddressResult>
methods.description: Resolves a PC-20 token (a token born ON Push Chain, mirrored outward as wrappers on external chains) against UniversalCore's on-chain registry, and lists every confirmed deployment. Accepts either end of the mapping — an external wrapper or the canonical Push-native token — and always returns the canonical token at .address, with every known deployment in .registry (confirmed only; a predicted first-export wrapper address never appears). Asynchronous, unlike getPRC20Address: PC-20 mappings are dynamic and live on chain. Never symbol-based — identity is address-and-chain only. options.chain is optional for lookup (SDK works out which chain the address belongs to; throws PC20AmbiguousAddressError if several chains claim it) but funds.token.chain is REQUIRED when spending. Resolve wrapper addresses from getPC20Address(...).registry — the authoritative record. receipt.externalAssetAddr is a best-effort mirror: the raw chain field is only observed when a wrapper is newly deployed, and although the SDK backfills it from UniversalCore it is undefined while an outbound is still in flight. Throws PC20WrapperNotRegisteredError, PC20RegistryMismatchError, PC20ExpectedButPRC20Error, PC20AmbiguousAddressError — see agents/errors.json for the full typed PC-20 error family.
methods.returns: Promise<{ address: `0x${string}`; name: string; symbol: string; decimals: number; network: PUSH_NETWORK; registry: Array<{ address: string; chain: CHAIN; chainName: string }> }>

methods.name: sendTransaction
methods.signature: pushChainClient.universal.sendTransaction(tx: { to, from?, value?, data?, funds?, progressHook?, gasLimit?, maxFeePerGas?, maxPriorityFeePerGas?, payGasWith?, deadline?, options?: { enforceGasCheck?: boolean } }): Promise<UniversalTxResponse>
methods.description: Sends universal transaction. Advanced args: gasLimit/maxFeePerGas/maxPriorityFeePerGas override gas; payGasWith pays fees in supported token; deadline sets execution expiry; options.enforceGasCheck (default false) — when true, the SDK throws InsufficientUEABalanceError on pre-flight gas/balance shortfall instead of emitting a WARNING progress event and proceeding. Solana targets use encodeTxData({ idl, functionName, args }) passed as tx.data — there is no svmExecute field. Multicall (outer tx.to = zero address, tx.data = Array<{to, value, data}>): from a native Push Chain EOA the batch executes atomically in a single EIP-7702 type-4 (SetCode) transaction when the signer supports signAuthorization (v6.0.19+; requires the batch executor to be deployed on the chain — Donut: yes, mainnet: not yet); if the signer cannot sign an authorization the SDK logs a warning and falls back to the legacy non-atomic sequential per-call loop before any broadcast. External-origin batches are unchanged and always atomic via UEA_MULTICALL. Every inner multicall entry must have a non-zero `to` (only the outer tx.to stays the zero address to signal multicall mode). The UniversalTxResponse includes `atomic: boolean` — false only when a native-EOA multicall fell back to sequential execution.

methods.name: prepareTransaction
methods.signature: pushChainClient.universal.prepareTransaction(tx: { to, from?, value?, data?, funds?, gasLimit?, maxFeePerGas?, maxPriorityFeePerGas?, payGasWith?, deadline?, options?: { enforceGasCheck?: boolean } }): Promise<PreparedUniversalTx>
methods.description: Prepares a transaction without executing it. Returns PreparedUniversalTx with route, estimatedGas, nonce, deadline, payload. Pass result to executeTransactions for multi-hop cascades. options.enforceGasCheck (default false) carries strict pre-flight gas/balance enforcement into executeTransactions — setting it on any single hop opts the entire cascade into strict mode.

methods.name: executeTransactions
methods.description: Executes ordered array of prepared transactions as a single-signature multi-hop cascade. Returns CascadedTxResponse with initialTxHash, hops[], hopCount, wait(opts?), waitForAll(opts?).

methods.name: trackTransaction
methods.signature: pushChainClient.universal.trackTransaction(txHash: string, options?: { chain?: CHAIN, progressHook?: (event: ProgressEvent) => void, waitForCompletion?: boolean, advanced?: { pollingIntervalMs?: number, timeout?: number, rpcUrls?: Partial<Record<CHAIN, string[]>> } }): Promise<UniversalTxResponse>
methods.description: Resumes tracking any universal transaction by hash and origin chain. Works independently of sendTransaction — pass any stored hash. Defaults chain to PUSH_TESTNET_DONUT. Set waitForCompletion:false for a snapshot status check without waiting. On Push Chain Donut, history-sensitive reads (transactions, receipts, universal-tx status) query the default pruned RPC first and automatically retry the archive endpoints on a pruned-history miss (v6.0.19+) — old transactions no longer fail to resolve; no new option needed.

arguments.name: txHash
arguments.description: Transaction hash on the origin chain

arguments.name: options.chain
arguments.description: Origin chain — defaults to PUSH_TESTNET_DONUT

arguments.name: options.progressHook
arguments.description: Callback invoked at each tracking step

arguments.name: options.waitForCompletion
arguments.description: true = poll until confirmed (default), false = return current status snapshot

arguments.name: options.advanced.pollingIntervalMs
arguments.description: Poll interval in ms (default 2000, min 500)

arguments.name: options.advanced.timeout
arguments.description: Max wait in ms before timeout (default 60000)

arguments.name: options.advanced.rpcUrls
arguments.description: Custom RPC URLs for status queries

methods.name: migrateCEA
methods.description: Migrates the Chain Executor Account (CEA) contract on an external chain to the latest implementation. Sends a MIGRATION_SELECTOR payload via Route 2. Pass the external chain whose CEA should be upgraded (e.g. PushChain.CONSTANTS.CHAIN.ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA).

methods.name: rescueFunds
methods.description: Recovers funds locked in the source-chain Vault after a CEA-to-Push (Route 3) inbound transaction fails, leaving the bridged tokens stuck. Triggers a manual TSS revert that releases them back to the user. universalTxId is the bytes32 hash of the failed inbound transaction; prc20 is the Push Chain PRC-20 token address whose source-chain counterpart is locked.

methods.name: signMessage
methods.description: Signs arbitrary message bytes

methods.description: Signs EIP-712 typed data

methods.name: read
methods.signature: pushChainClient.universal.read(subject: string, options: { chain: CHAIN, token?: string, abi?: any[], idl?: any, functionName?: string, args?: any[], storageSlot?: bigint | Hex, web2?: { extract: Array<{ path: string, valueType: 'uint256' | 'int256' | 'bool' | 'string' | 'bytes', decimals?: number }>, method?: 'GET' | 'POST', headers?: Record<string, string>, body?: string | Uint8Array, timeoutMs?: number }, callback?: { target: string, gasLimit: bigint, abi: Abi, functionName: string, args?: (spec, gasLimit) => unknown[] }, waitForCompletion?: boolean, progressHook?: (progress: ProgressEvent) => void, blockNumber?: bigint, minConfirmations?: number, expiryBlocks?: bigint, maxFee?: bigint, refundTo?: string, advanced?: { pollingIntervalMs?: number, timeout?: number, enforceGasCheck?: boolean } }): Promise<UniversalReadResponse>
methods.description: Requests state from an EVM chain, Solana or an HTTPS endpoint and has validators deliver the agreed result on-chain to Push Chain: to the Universal Read Registry (0x00000000000000000000000000000000000000b2, the default) or to your own UniversalReadClient receiver via callback. One query option picks the read: none = native balance, token = ERC-20 or SPL balance, abi or idl + functionName (+ args) = typed contract call or Solana program account, storageSlot = EVM storage word, web2 = JSON fields from an HTTPS endpoint (chain: CHAIN.WEB2). Paid and asynchronous. outcome is the success signal: READ.OUTCOME.SUCCESS means value is usable; any other outcome names the failure (status, raw.status, callbackDelivered and decodeError are debugging fields). Response: requestId, requestIdUint (bigint), txHash, chain, outcome (READ.OUTCOME), status (READ.STATUS), isTerminal, callbackDelivered, callbackFailReason, value, decodeError, raw { status, resultData, errorCode }, errorMsg, fees, request, pcTx, explorerUrl, wait(), refresh().

arguments.name: subject
arguments.description: What to read: an account address for a balance, a contract address for a contract call or storage slot, or a URL for a Web2 read. Solana subjects are base58.

arguments.name: options.chain
arguments.description: Where to read from: any supported EVM or Solana chain, or CHAIN.WEB2 for an HTTPS endpoint. Pass at most one query option; with none, read returns the subject's native balance.

arguments.name: options.token
arguments.description: Web3 chains. Token balance of subject. EVM: the ERC-20 contract address, read via balanceOf. Solana: the SPL mint address; the SDK derives the associated token account.

arguments.name: options.abi | options.idl
arguments.description: abi (EVM only): an ABI array; the call is encoded and value decoded and typed from it. Any mutability is accepted: validators run the call as an eth_call simulation at the pinned block, so nonpayable/payable functions return data and never execute. idl (Solana only): an Anchor IDL object; the subject account is decoded with the layout whose 8-byte discriminator matches its data. Reads never execute an instruction. abi on Solana or idl on EVM is rejected (INVALID_READ_QUERY).

arguments.name: options.functionName
arguments.description: With abi: the function to call (required). With idl: the account layout name (optional; inferred from the discriminator when omitted; snake_case, camelCase or the IDL's PascalCase accepted); passing it types value at compile time. accountName is not supported and throws.

arguments.name: options.args
arguments.description: With abi: positional call arguments. With idl: allowed only when subject is the program id; they are the non-constant PDA seeds of functionName's account, in the order the IDL declares them (pubkey: base58, 0x-hex 32-byte string or PublicKey; integers: bigint; also bool, string, bytes). The seed count must match.

arguments.name: options.storageSlot
arguments.description: EVM only. One storage word from the subject contract.

arguments.name: options.web2
arguments.description: Required when chain is CHAIN.WEB2. extract: 1 to 16 entries of { path (JSONPath), valueType ('uint256' | 'int256' | 'bool' | 'string' | 'bytes'), decimals? }; results come back as an array in the same order. method defaults to GET; body is POST only; timeoutMs defaults to 5000. URL, headers and body are written to a public event log, so never include secrets.

arguments.name: options.callback
arguments.description: Routes the request through your own receiver contract (inherits UniversalReadClient) instead of the Universal Read Registry. target, abi and functionName are required together; gasLimit is the gas for _onReadResult (optional, default 500_000n for the registry and custom targets, at most 1_000_000n); functionName is the payable request entrypoint, which must emit exactly one ReadRequested per prepared read; args maps (spec, gasLimit) onto a different entrypoint argument order.

arguments.name: options.waitForCompletion
arguments.description: Default true. false resolves once the request is confirmed on Push Chain and indexed by the node (up to 30 s; ReadNotFoundError / READ_NOT_FOUND after that, with the request already paid), before validators vote; call wait() on the response to finish.

arguments.name: options.progressHook
arguments.description: Progress events READ-TX-101 through READ-TX-199-03 (see agents/workflows/progress-hook-events.md). READ-TX-199-01 fires only when outcome is SUCCESS; other terminal outcomes end on READ-TX-199-02.

arguments.name: options.blockNumber
arguments.description: EVM only. Pins the read to a destination block. Default: oracle height minus minConfirmations.

arguments.name: options.minConfirmations
arguments.description: EVM only. Confirmations the destination block must have. Default 1.

arguments.name: options.expiryBlocks
arguments.description: Request lifetime in Push Chain blocks. Default 300n. An unfulfilled request expires and refunds the unused callback budget.

arguments.name: options.maxFee
arguments.description: Cap on the upfront payment (protocol fee plus callback budget). Default: SDK estimated.

arguments.name: options.refundTo
arguments.description: Where unused callback budget is sent. Default: your Push account. Must accept native transfers.

arguments.name: options.advanced.pollingIntervalMs
arguments.description: Milliseconds between status polls. Default 2000, minimum 500.

arguments.name: options.advanced.timeout
arguments.description: Maximum milliseconds this caller waits. Default derived from expiry, at most 180000. Timing out does not cancel the request; resume with trackRead.

arguments.name: options.advanced.enforceGasCheck
arguments.description: Default false: warn and proceed when the pre-flight balance check finds a shortfall. true throws before broadcasting.

methods.name: prepareRead
methods.signature: pushChainClient.universal.prepareRead(subject: string, options: { chain: CHAIN, token? | abi? | idl? + functionName? + args? | storageSlot? | web2?, callback?, blockNumber?, minConfirmations?, expiryBlocks?, maxFee?, refundTo? }): Promise<PreparedRead>
methods.description: Prepares a read without executing it: nothing is broadcast and nothing is paid, so no funds are needed. Takes the same subject and query options as read, but not waitForCompletion, progressHook or advanced (those belong to executeReads). Returns PreparedRead { queryKey, chain, spec, specTuple, encodedSpec, value, fees { protocolFee, callbackBudget, total }, callbackGasLimit, callback, resultShape, preflight, warnings }. value (equal to fees.total) is the msg.value the request carries; specTuple is the positional ReadSpec for a hand-built call to your own entrypoint.

methods.name: executeReads
methods.signature: pushChainClient.universal.executeReads(preparedReads: PreparedRead[], options?: { waitForCompletion?: boolean, progressHook?: (progress: ProgressEvent) => void, advanced?: { pollingIntervalMs?: number, timeout?: number, enforceGasCheck?: boolean } }): Promise<BatchReadResponse>
methods.description: Executes an ordered array of prepared reads as one flow: a single transaction (one signature) where the wallet supports atomic batching, otherwise sequential transactions listed in transactionHashes. Returns BatchReadResponse { txHash, transactionHashes, reads, count, atomic, wait() }; wait() returns the UniversalReadResponse array in prepared order. atomic describes submission only; validators fulfill each read on its own, so check value on every response. With sequential submission, check the hashes on an error before resubmitting.

arguments.name: preparedReads
arguments.description: Reads returned by prepareRead. Results come back in this order.

arguments.name: options.waitForCompletion
arguments.description: Default true. false returns once the requests are submitted; call wait() to finish.

arguments.name: options.progressHook
arguments.description: Batch events READ-TX-001 to READ-TX-999-03 plus each read's own READ-TX-1xx events.

arguments.name: options.advanced.pollingIntervalMs
arguments.description: Milliseconds between status polls. Default 2000, minimum 500.

arguments.name: options.advanced.timeout
arguments.description: Maximum milliseconds this caller waits. Timing out cancels nothing.

arguments.name: options.advanced.enforceGasCheck
arguments.description: true throws before broadcasting when the balance check finds a shortfall.

methods.name: trackRead
methods.signature: pushChainClient.universal.trackRead({ requestId } | { txHash }, options?: { resultShape?: { kind: 'evmCall', abi, functionName } | ..., progressHook?: (progress: ProgressEvent) => void, advanced?: { pollingIntervalMs?: number, timeout?: number } }): Promise<UniversalReadResponse | UniversalReadResponse[]>
methods.description: Returns the current state of a read by its request ID (hex or numeric), or of every read submitted by a Push Chain transaction (an array, since one transaction can carry several reads). Works with a read-only client that has no signer and no funds, from any session. Call wait() on a snapshot to poll to a terminal status, or refresh() for one fresh snapshot. Balances, storage and Web2 reads decode automatically; pass resultShape to decode a typed contract call resumed in a new session. A wait() timeout throws ReadTimeoutError (code READ_TIMEOUT) and cancels nothing.

arguments.name: ref.requestId | ref.txHash
arguments.description: The read's request ID (0x-hex or bigint), or the Push Chain transaction that submitted it. Pass one. The lookup retries for up to 30 s while the node indexes the request, then throws ReadNotFoundError (code READ_NOT_FOUND): retry with the same reference, never resubmit.

arguments.name: options.resultShape
arguments.description: How to decode resultData. Inferred for balances, storage and Web2; a typed contract call resumed in a new session needs it, or value stays raw bytes.

arguments.name: options.progressHook
arguments.description: Invoked during the lookup (READ-TX-104-03/04/05), on refresh(), and at each lifecycle step while wait() polls.

arguments.name: options.advanced.pollingIntervalMs
arguments.description: Milliseconds between polls, during the lookup and in wait(). Default 2000, minimum 500.

arguments.name: options.advanced.timeout
arguments.description: Maximum milliseconds wait() polls before throwing ReadTimeoutError (code READ_TIMEOUT, with lastStatus, requestId, txHash). Default derived from expiry, at most 180000. Does not change the 30 s lookup window. snapshot.wait() also takes flat { timeoutMs, pollingIntervalMs, resultShape }; trackRead options carry into it.

exports.name: usePushChainClient
exports.description: Returns the initialized PushChainClient (from @pushchain/core) after wallet connection. Exposes all core transaction methods: sendTransaction, signMessage, prepareTransaction, executeTransactions, and the Universal Read methods read, prepareRead, executeReads and trackRead. This is the primary way to execute universal transactions in a React app. Note on multicall: browser wallets connect as JSON-RPC accounts and cannot sign EIP-7702 authorizations, so a native-Push-EOA batch sent from the browser falls back to sequential (non-atomic) execution; check response.atomic to see which path ran. Push Wallet email/google logins and backend local-key signers can use the atomic path.
